title: Refusal direction
description: Removing or adding an activation direction changes refusal behavior.

coverage.scope_note: This snapshot contains the saved merged final records used by this entry, including records not individually shown on the page. It is not an exhaustive collection of experiments or papers. Missing records, omitted extraction and not-tested statements are different from negative results.

claims.heading: A harmful-minus-harmless activation direction can reduce or induce refusal
Removing the refusal direction from model weights can suppress refusal
Jailbreaks can suppress the refusal direction; training against ablation can improve robustness
Refusal can involve a dominant direction plus additional directions
Harmfulness judgments can be encoded separately from refusal decisions
Refusal directions can transfer across languages and model variants
Training shapes whether refusal depends on one removable direction
Single-direction refusal control in reasoning models remains contested

related_findings.title: Small component sets can change refusal
related_findings.summary: Editing selected weight rows or experts can change refusal more than random edits. Single-head patching rarely reverses over-refusal.

examples.headline: Zeroing attribution-selected weight rows increases harmful-prompt refusal more than layer-matched random masks.
Single-head patching rarely reverses over-refusal in LLaMA-3.1-8B.
Suppressing gradient-ranked experts usually cut refusal more than activation-ranked or random selection.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Refusal removal changes other behaviour
related_findings.summary: Weight edits can preserve standard benchmark scores while changing truthfulness, optimism, confidence and other behaviour. These effects vary across models and tools, and small output-distribution shifts do not guarantee coherence.

examples.headline: Abliteration lowers TruthfulQA performance while barely changing MMLU, HellaSwag and IFEval.
Abliteration increases optimism in Gemma and Qwen but moves confidence in opposite directions.
ICONOCLAST matches or lowers HERETIC's residual refusal, usually with less output-distribution drift.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Jailbreaks use several routes around refusal
related_findings.summary: Suppressing the refusal-direction projection can improve jailbreak attacks, but does not always produce useful compliance. Other attacks involve changes outside the direction estimated from single-turn prompts.

examples.headline: Adding refusal-direction suppression improves GCG attack success and transfer from Llama-3 to Vicuna-v1.5.
Lowering the refusal projection leaves useful compliance at noise level in Qwen 7B.
Multi-turn drift lies mostly outside the refusal-harmfulness plane, but removing it does not reduce harmful compliance.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Refusal scores have limited monitoring reliability
related_findings.summary: Projection scores can distinguish realized refusals from compliance and clarification. Harmful-prompt classification can weaken under jailbreaks and topic matching, and calibration errors can remain after recalibration.

examples.headline: A frozen direction score separates refusals from compliance and clarification on benign Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct responses.
Refusal-direction prompt classification performs near or below chance on WildJailbreak.
Mean-difference readouts lose discrimination on matched topics and retain calibration errors after recalibration.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Geometry and refusal can change separately
related_findings.summary: Fine-tuning can shift or compress refusal representations alongside behavioural changes. Quantization and uncensoring also show that similar direction geometry can coexist with substantially weaker refusal.

examples.headline: AWQ and GPTQ preserve direction cosine while refusal falls on hidden-danger prompts.
DarkIdol largely complies despite retained harmful-prompt separation; direction cosine is not reported.
Supervised fine-tuning compresses refusal representations, while reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards largely preserves them.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Refusal overlaps other ways of withholding answers
related_findings.summary: Abstention, hedging and other non-answering behaviours have directions that are largely distinct from safety refusal. Partial overlap still allows interventions on these behaviours to affect harmful-prompt refusal.

examples.headline: Hedge-direction ablation makes answers more direct while changing harmful-prompt refusal little.
Reversing benign-derived abstention steering breaks safety refusal, partly through its refusal-direction component.
Safety-refusal probes transfer to knowledge refusal better than knowledge-refusal probes transfer to safety refusal.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Text directions transfer unevenly across modalities
related_findings.summary: Text-derived directions can support refusal interventions on image-text inputs. Harmful images can activate aligned directions less strongly than equivalent text, while subtracting image-conditioning shifts can restore refusal.

examples.headline: Text safety probes weaken on image-text inputs, yet text-derived steering reduces multimodal attack success.
Image-conditioning shifts align with the text refusal direction; subtracting them usually restores refusal.
Harmful images activate aligned refusal directions less strongly than equivalent text and receive fewer refusals.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Safety steering trades refusal against usefulness
related_findings.summary: Adding refusal vectors can reduce harmful compliance, with effects that vary by model and intervention. Unconditional steering can increase benign refusals and reduce capability; gating can reduce capability costs.

examples.headline: Refusal-vector addition improves harmful noncompliance but harms benign performance; gating reduces capability costs.
DeSteer reduces jailbreak success but increases Vicuna's false refusals and lowers conversational benchmark scores.
Unit-normalized contrastive steering leaves jailbreak success and over-refusal near baseline, with little data-scaling benefit.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Direction estimates depend on experimental choices
related_findings.summary: Contrast baselines, labels and direction construction affect intervention results, which also vary across models. Estimator reliability provides a baseline for interpreting similarity between independently estimated directions.

examples.headline: Control contrasts reveal label insensitivity, contrast reversals and inflated KL differences from placeholder wording.
Split-half direction similarity closely matches the predicted estimator noise floor in Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct.
Which estimated direction reduces refusal under single-layer ablation varies across Llama, Mistral-v0.2 and Qwen.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Several interventions can control refusal
related_findings.summary: Learned rotations and nonlinear maps can change refusal. A learned nonlinear map bypasses refusal with smaller edits than mean-difference ablation. Response-contrast vectors perform unevenly and can match or underperform random directions.

examples.headline: Learned subspace rotations can increase or suppress unsafe responses while largely preserving measured capability.
A learned nonlinear map bypasses refusal with smaller edits than mean-difference ablation.
Response-contrast refusal vectors show uneven performance, sometimes matching or underperforming random directions.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Resistance to ablation depends on the attack
related_findings.summary: Training and decoy edits can block standard refusal-direction ablation. Adaptive or higher-rank attacks sometimes recover compliance, and some apparent protection comes with severe output degradation.

examples.headline: Nonlinear decoys block standard ablation, but adaptive and higher-rank attacks recover substantial success.
Ablation-resistant training blocks standard attacks, sometimes through degeneration; adaptive ablation still bypasses Qwen-2.5-72B.
Unchecked results report compliance-reward fine-tuning removing refusal from defended Qwen3-14B without direction edits.

related_findings.title: Post-training reshapes existing harm representations
related_findings.summary: Base models already represent distinctions between harmful and benign prompts. Post-training can amplify these distinctions and create or strengthen refusal mechanisms, with geometry shaped by the training objective.

examples.headline: Harmful-prompt clustering is much stronger in tuned models than in their base counterparts.
Qwen preserves safety-neuron write columns while amplifying activation differences; a Llama neuron is rewritten.
Base-trained safety probes retain similar accuracy in successors despite rotation of mean-difference directions.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Other behaviours also admit directional interventions
related_findings.summary: Contrastive directions can change honesty, persona and sentiment, extending the intervention pattern beyond refusal. A direction that predicts behaviour does not necessarily control it.

examples.headline: Contrastive steering increases honesty under instructions to lie, while direction removal has mixed effects.
Adding an assistant-persona direction reduces jailbreak-induced persona changes; subtracting it increases them.
Sentiment-direction ablation reduces Pythia-2.8b classification accuracy far more than random-direction ablation.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Refusal shares structure across topics
related_findings.summary: Category-specific refusal directions share substantial structure, and removing one category's representation can affect others. Selective removal of political refusal works in some models through topic concepts or other targeted interventions.

examples.headline: Domain refusal directions align with a universal direction and reduce refusal across domains unevenly.
Removing category subspaces changes refusal elsewhere and can increase refusal in Gemma.
Erasing political concepts reduces political refusal; masking political intent has model-dependent effects.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Targeted steering can reduce over-refusal
related_findings.summary: Gated repairs can reduce false refusals and limit newly harmful replies compared with ungated edits. Repairs can mostly preserve safety on direct harmful queries while weakening it under jailbreak prefixes.

examples.headline: Gating an over-refusal repair sharply reduces newly harmful replies compared with the ungated edit.
Subtracting a mean-difference vector only on classified-benign prompts reduces false refusal.
Over-refusal repairs mostly preserve direct harmful-query safety but weaken safety against jailbreak prefixes.

related_findings.title: Chat refusal only partly governs agent actions
related_findings.summary: Chat-derived refusal signals can weaken in tool and agent settings, with transfer varying across models. Restoring the signal reverses only some unsafe calls. Low-rank activation patching can change prompt-injection compliance.

examples.headline: Tool contexts weaken refusal activation; restoring it reverses only some unsafe calls.
A chat-derived direction separates agent prompts in Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct but performs near chance in Mistral-7B-Instruct.
Low-rank patching changes prompt-injection compliance, with larger subspaces needed for Qwen3-32B.

related_findings.title: Models can recognize harm while complying
related_findings.summary: Harmfulness can remain readable or explicitly reportable after training that weakens refusal. This supports a separation between recognizing harm and refusing.

examples.headline: Acceptance fine-tuning leaves harmfulness separation largely unchanged; adding a harmfulness direction can induce refusal.
Harmfully trained models still recognize policy violations, and reflection prompting reduces their harmful responses.
Reversing the order of refusal and harm-detection interventions sharply changes attack success.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Reasoning changes when refusal signals appear
related_findings.summary: Refusal signals vary across the prompt, thinking process and answer transition. Reasoning can strengthen or suppress them, making extraction position and reasoning-specific components important for interpreting interventions.

examples.headline: Self-jailbreaking reasoning increases compliance projection and lowers perceived harmfulness.
Refusal scores drop at thinking-end tokens; ablating negatively contributing heads reduces harmful output.
Harmful and benign representations separate more at forced answer tags than before reasoning.

related_findings.title: Accurate decoding does not establish causal control
related_findings.summary: Directions and layers that distinguish harmful from benign prompts need not control refusal. Near-perfect classification can coexist with weak ablation effects or effects indistinguishable from random interventions.

examples.headline: Harmfulness is highly decodable at a layer where ablation barely changes the refusal margin.
Near-perfect linear separation does not make ablation effective on INSEP.
Perfectly classifying Gemma directions have ablation effects within the random-null band.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Refusal depends on positions and computational pathways
related_findings.summary: Refusal signals appear at post-instruction template positions and across multiple layers. Steering effects propagate mainly through attention value/output and MLP pathways, with less dependence on attention patterns.

examples.headline: Freezing attention patterns barely changes steering; disrupting value/output or MLP pathways weakens it substantially.
Removing post-instruction template tokens lowers substring-scored refusal across Llama2, Llama3 and Qwen2.
Layer-specific ablation still bypasses refusal when layer 12 is skipped, despite different refusal scores.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Language affects refusal signals and transfer
related_findings.summary: Separation and intervention transfer can weaken in lower-resource languages, while language-specific directions can still classify harmfulness well. Features correlated with English refusal may lose significance or reverse sign in other languages.

examples.headline: Weaker harmful-benign separation across languages tracks weaker intervention transfer.
Arabic-derived directions distinguish harmful from benign prompts, with model-specific score scales and thresholds.
English refusal-correlated features mostly lose significance in Japanese, Spanish and Dutch; some reverse sign.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Evaluation choices change measured refusal
related_findings.summary: Scorers and decoding can change measured refusal and bypass rates. Refusal-language removal, coherent compliance and actionable harmful content require distinct evaluation.

examples.headline: Single-neuron refusal bypass does not consistently yield actionable harmful content.
Repeated temperature sampling finds harmful outputs far more often than greedy decoding.
LLM judges misclassify transcript refusals more often when partial action precedes refusal.

related_findings.title: Unrelated steering can weaken refusal
related_findings.summary: Trait steering and generic activation perturbations can increase harmful compliance. Alignment with the refusal direction predicts some effects, but removing that component can leave substantial vulnerability.

examples.headline: Trait-vector alignment with the refusal direction predicts attack success in Llama-3.1-8B.
Removing refusal components from unrelated steering vectors modestly reduces attacks but leaves substantial vulnerability.
Random Gaussian perturbations injected at intermediate layers can bypass refusal and improve subsequent GCG attacks.

related_findings.title: Early output tokens help mediate refusal
related_findings.summary: Early refusal-token logits provide both intervention targets and monitoring signals. Penalizing refusal tokens or fragmenting input tokens can bypass refusal, while logit-based stopping can reduce attack success.

examples.headline: Penalizing refusal tokens and rewarding compliance tokens achieves high judged attack success with retries.
Greedy space insertion usually flips the first-token refusal logit gap across tested models.
An early-stop rule based on refusal-dominant logits reduces jailbreak success without format-free benign false positives.

related_findings.title: Weight edits can leave refusal behind
related_findings.summary: A single projection pass may leave substantial refusal-related separation. Low-bit editing reports also show sensitivity to how edited weights are stored, and refusal scores can change differently on harmful and harmless prompts.

examples.headline: A single rank-one weight projection reduces but does not eliminate Qwen2.5-0.5B's refusal margin.
Keeping edited GLM-5.3 Flash output projections in BF16 improves an undefined evaluation metric.
Gemma abliteration lowers refusal scores much more on harmless prompts than harmful prompts.

related_findings.title: Cross-model transfer benefits from representation alignment
related_findings.summary: Refusal directions from independently trained models have little raw alignment. Explicit representation maps can transport refusal interventions or harmfulness probes, although successful classification transfer does not itself establish causal transfer.

examples.headline: Harmful-minus-harmless direction fingerprints have near-zero cosine across independently trained models.
Signed permutation preserves cross-seed refusal steering, while permutation alone reverses its effect.
Rotation-transported harm probes match Falcon-Mamba's own probe, with less diagnostic evidence for RWKV and Zamba2.

related_findings.title: Unrelated activation changes can induce refusal
related_findings.summary: Steering emotion, hostility or unrelated behaviours can increase refusal in safety-trained models. Some effects persist after removing the refusal-direction component, suggesting refusal can serve as a fallback response.

examples.headline: Political-hostility steering can increase refusal even after its refusal-direction component is removed.
Emotion-vector steering increases Llama's HarmBench refusal across several emotions.
Unrelated steering often induces refusal, with strong variation across model families.

related_findings.title: Distillation can transmit reduced refusal
related_findings.summary: Students can inherit reduced refusal from edited or steered teachers through benign or unrelated training outputs. Some studies measure other harmful behaviour, and low coherence can complicate refusal judgments.

examples.headline: Students trained on benign teacher responses inherit increased harmful compliance above a steering threshold.
Unrelated abliterated-teacher rollouts reduce student refusal on China-sensitive questions, with coherence concerns.
Students distilled from ablated-teacher transcripts choose harmful agentic shortcuts more often than controls.

related_findings.title: Directional ablation can reverse some unlearning
related_findings.summary: Removing contrastive directions can recover knowledge suppressed by some unlearning methods. Recovery is incomplete or absent in other settings, and the effective directions need not be refusal directions.

examples.headline: Per-layer mean-difference ablation recovers WMDP-Bio performance after several unlearning methods.
Jointly ablating bio and cyber junk directions partially recovers Zephyr_RMU's suppressed knowledge.
Refusal-direction ablation fails to recover WMDP-Bio performance after ILU-RMU.

related_findings.title: Directional safety interventions extend beyond language models
related_findings.summary: Supervised safety directions and contrastive weight edits can reduce classifier- or judge-rated unsafe video generation. These results provide analogues of directional intervention outside language models.

examples.headline: Adding a supervised safety direction improves classifier-rated safety across tested video diffusion models.
Low-rank edits from unsafe-safe prompt contrasts reduce judged unsafe video generation.
Embedding a mean-difference concept vector into video-diffusion MLP weights reduces unsafe generations.

related_findings.title: Inducing and removing refusal need different interventions
related_findings.summary: Installing refusal and releasing a withheld answer can require different positions and intervention strengths. Which operation is easier varies across studies and settings.

examples.headline: Single-position patching releases withheld answers, while reimposing refusal requires sensitive multi-position patches.
Single-token steering installs instructed refusal more effectively than it removes it in Gemma 2 2B-IT.
An informal report describes effective refusal steering but failed compliance steering, without rates.

related_findings.title: Backdoor directions overlap broader refusal representations
related_findings.summary: Backdoor behaviour can be mediated by residual directions that overlap the refusal subspace beyond its leading direction.

examples.headline: Resetting backdoor-direction projections closes much of the triggered compliance-refusal score gap.
Backdoor directions overlap broader refusal subspaces more strongly than the leading refusal direction alone.

reading_list.why: Introduces mean-difference refusal ablation and addition across chat models, with weight-edit results showing system-prompt sensitivity.
Tests removal, induction and base-to-instruct transfer, showing strong model dependence and limits to causal transfer.
Tests single-direction removal on a 320B MoE with random controls, capability checks and incomplete category-level removal.

known_gaps.summary: The main gaps concern verified independent evidence, matched intervention comparisons, larger-model robustness, multilingual coverage and the distinction between readable signals and causal control.
items: Some findings on defended models and large-model refusal removal rely on a study whose results remain unverified.

Reasoning-model comparisons mix activation ablation, per-expert weight edits and different direction definitions. Matched experiments are needed to distinguish method sensitivity from genuine replication failures or model-size effects.
The larger-model evidence for training against ablation remains incompletely assessed. Robustness to prompt-based jailbreaks and robustness to direct direction removal need separate conclusions.
Independent replication is uncertain for some findings because author overlap and multiple reports of the same work remain unresolved.
Potential disagreements involving the same model and intervention have not all been examined. The causes of inconsistent refusal-removal results remain unresolved.
Language coverage remains uncertain after accounting for existing multilingual removal experiments. The evidence does not yet establish which language conditions lack intervention tests.
For some model families, evidence that harmfulness is readable still needs to be distinguished from evidence that intervening on it controls refusal.
